meta.title: Etherbit Tiling — The invisible fabric that puts your windows in perfect orbit
meta.description: Automatic window manager (tiling) with an OS-agnostic algorithm in Rust. Native support for macOS (Swift) and Linux — GNOME 45+ and KDE Plasma 6 (Wayland). Zero wasted space, automatic organization.
hero.subtitle: The invisible fabric that puts your windows in perfect orbit.
hero.mockupAria: Demo: windows organizing themselves automatically into blocks
hero.mockupCaption: Ether Flow organizing space in real time
manifesto.lead: The name is the surgical fusion of two concepts — physics and computing — that define the soul of the algorithm. Together, they create a unique productivity experience, independent of the operating system.
manifesto.etherBody: In classical physics, the Ether was the invisible substance that filled all of space. Here, Ether is the mathematical filling of pixels: an invisible fabric that arranges windows into blocks so that every pixel of the screen is used edge to edge, with no gaps and no overlaps.
manifesto.bitTitle: Bit — the gravity of the orbit
manifesto.bitBody: The suffix Bit inherits the mechanics of Orbit: the perfect balance where windows find their ideal positions on their own, guided by the system's computational gravity. And it celebrates the bit as the unit of computing — a focus on pure, native performance.
pillars.dynamicBody: Opened a terminal, an editor or the browser? The window snaps into the right orbit instantly. No mouse.
pillars.flowBody: Mathematical screen division, platform-agnostic, that eliminates dead space and adapts in real time.
pillars.nativeBody: Built on the most stable APIs of each OS. Light, fast, and it doesn't break with every update.

diag.title: Report Problems & Diagnostics
diag.lead: Found a bug? Generate a clean log file with a single command, then attach it to your report. Pick the block for your desktop and the scenario that fits.
diag.gnomeAHint: Filters the GNOME extension output from the last hour and merges the Core telemetry (if present). Saves to your Downloads folder.
diag.gnomeBHint: Same filters, but the full history since the last system boot. Use it when the issue happened earlier in this session.
diag.kdeAHint: Isolates the KWin and Etherbit engine logs from the last two hours and merges the Core telemetry (if present). Saves to your Downloads folder.
diag.kdeBHint: Same filters, but the full history since the last system boot. Use it when the issue happened earlier in this session.
diag.step2: Copy and run the command for your desktop environment and chosen scenario.
diag.step3: Find the log file generated automatically in your Downloads folder.
diag.step4: Click Report Bug to open an issue in our repository and attach the extracted file.

uninstall.note: Your configuration is preserved by default. The files ~/.config/etherbit-tiling/ and (on GNOME) ~/.config/autostart/etherbit.tiling@ediano.dev.desktop are not removed. To delete them too, run the uninstaller with ETHERBIT_PURGE=1 or remove them by hand. On Wayland: on GNOME, log out/in to unload the extension; on KDE, qdbus … reconfigure already unloads the KWin Script.
